Marathon Petroleum rallied 0.44% today to $414.65, extending a sharp recovery from last week's lows. The stock has climbed nearly $42 in four trading days, driven by a tightening supply picture for refined products: heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year as winter approaches and demand surges, while diesel and heating oil inventories remain relatively lean at 103.33 million barrels. Refineries operating at 95.2% capacity are working to meet this seasonal demand, which supports prices and margins for refiners like Marathon.

The broader context is a shift in oil market dynamics away from the surplus that emerged in recent weeks. Russian crude production has rebounded following geopolitical developments, yet global supply-demand balance appears to be tightening again as winter heating demand picks up—a seasonal tailwind for refinery profitability that typically persists through early 2027.
